Rashi on Shabbat 20a:1:1.hebrew: ובגבולין - צריך להבעיר מדורתן מבעוד יום, כדי שתאחוז האש ברובו:
Rashi on Shabbat 20a:1:1.english: And in the outlying areas - One must light their bonfire while it is still day, so that the fire takes hold of most of it.

Rashi on Shabbat 20a:1:2.hebrew: ר' יהודה אומר - אם היתה מדורת פחמין, אין צריך להאחיז בהן האור אלא כל שהוא, והיא דולקת והולכת, דאין דרכה להיות כבה והולכת, וא"צ לחתות בהן:
Rashi on Shabbat 20a:1:2.english: Rabbi Yehuda says - If it was a bonfire of coals, one does not need to kindle the fire in them except in any amount, and it continues to burn; for it is not its nature to progressively go out, and one does not need to stoke them.

Rashi on Shabbat 20a:2:1.hebrew: בן דרוסאי - לסטים היה, ומבשל בישולו שליש:
Rashi on Shabbat 20a:2:1.english: Ben Drosai - He was a bandit, and would cook his food [only] one-third [done].

Rashi on Shabbat 20a:2:2.english: It was also stated - That the food of ben Drosai is considered cooked.

Rashi on Shabbat 20a:2:3.hebrew: כל שהוא - מבושל ביד ישראל כמאכל בן דרוסאי, שוב אין בגמרו משום בישולי נכרים:
Rashi on Shabbat 20a:2:3.english: Anything that is - Cooked by the hand of an Israelite like the food of ben Drosai — there is no longer in its completion [by a gentile any prohibition of] food cooked by gentiles.

Rashi on Shabbat 20a:2:4.english: Swept - [Cleared] of the coals with a shovel, which they call vadil [a baker's shovel].

Rashi on Shabbat 20a:2:5.hebrew: קטום - מפזרים אפר מלמעלה כדי להפיג חומו, שלא יוסיף הבל בשבת. וזה — תבשיל שהוא כמאכל בן דרוסאי — לא חיישי' אם מתבשל והולך בשבת:
Rashi on Shabbat 20a:2:5.english: Covered [with ashes] - One scatters ashes on top in order to reduce its heat, so that it will not add heat on Shabbat. And [in] this [case] — a dish that is [cooked] like the food of ben Drosai — we are not concerned if it continues to cook on Shabbat.

Rashi on Shabbat 20a:3:1.hebrew: דגבי תנור - שהככרות נדבקים בדופני התנור סביב. הילכך, מבעיא ליה: הי קרי תחתון — הנך פנים דגבי דופני התנור, או פנים הפונים למטה לחלל התנור לצד האור:
Rashi on Shabbat 20a:3:1.english: [That side] close to the oven - For the loaves are stuck to the walls of the oven all around. Therefore, the dilemma was raised: Which [surface] does he call "bottom" — that surface which is close to the walls of the oven, or the surface that faces downward into the cavity of the oven, toward the fire?

Rashi on Shabbat 20a:3:2.hebrew: מדובקים בתנור - וחומרא היא, דפנים שכלפי האור ממהרין לקרום:
Rashi on Shabbat 20a:3:2.english: Stuck to the oven - And this is a stringency, for the surface facing the fire forms a crust more quickly.

Rashi on Shabbat 20a:4:1.hebrew: התם מנתח - ואם פותח פי התנור, עייל ביה זיקא וקשי ליה:
Rashi on Shabbat 20a:4:1.english: There, it is cut into pieces - And if he opens the mouth of the oven, a draft enters it and harms it [the meat].

Rashi on Shabbat 20a:4:2.hebrew: הכא לא מנתח - דכתיב (שמות י״ב:ט׳) על ראשו ועל קרבו, ואי מגלי ליה, לא קשי ליה זיקא. הלכך, אי לא דזריזין הן, אסור:
Rashi on Shabbat 20a:4:2.english: Here it is not cut into pieces - As it is written (Exodus 12:9): “its head with its innards,” and if he uncovers it, the draft does not harm it. Therefore, were it not that they are vigilant, [it would be] forbidden.

Rashi on Shabbat 20a:5:1.hebrew: אברים ופדרים הוא דאתא - להתיר את הקטירן כל הלילה; אבל מדורת בית המוקד, שאינה צורך גבוה אלא צורך כהנים, לא הותרה. וסמוך לחשיכה, היינו טעמא דלא גזור — משום דכהנים זריזין הם, שכולם היו בני תורה וחרדים ונזכרים, ולא אתו לחתויי משתחשך:
Rashi on Shabbat 20a:5:1.english: It was [for] limbs and fats that it came - To permit burning them all night; but the bonfire of the Chamber of the Hearth, which is not for the need of the Most High but rather for the need of the priests, was not permitted [on Shabbat]. And [regarding kindling it] adjacent to nightfall, this is the reason that they did not decree [against it]: Because priests are vigilant, for they were all Torah scholars, scrupulous, and mindful, and they will not come to stoke [the coals] once it gets dark.

Rashi on Shabbat 20a:6:1.hebrew: כל אחד ואחד - כל עץ ועץ, ולא תימא כיון שאחזה ברוב מנין העצים:
Rashi on Shabbat 20a:6:1.english: Each and every one - Each and every piece of wood; and do not say that once [the fire] has taken hold in the majority of the number of pieces of wood [it is sufficient].

Rashi on Shabbat 20a:6:2.english: And Shmuel said - So that one need not say: "Bring thin pieces of wood and let us place [them] beneath them to ignite these."

Rashi on Shabbat 20a:6:3.hebrew: תני ר' חייא - בפ' במה מדליקין, לגבי מנורה: "להעלות נר תמיד" — שתהא שלהבת עולה מאליה; אלמא, בכי האי גוונא הויא הדלקה — משום ר"י הלוי. וקשה לי: חדא, דרמי בר חמא קתני לה התם; ועוד, דלאו מתניתא היא, אלא הוא אמר לה בפירוש דמתני' אחריתי. ושאר רבותינו תנו לה לענין מדורה, ואני מצאתי אותה בת"כ לגבי מנורה:
Rashi on Shabbat 20a:6:3.english: Rav Ḥiyya taught - [Rav Ḥiyya taught this] in the chapter [entitled] Bameh Madlikin regarding the [Temple] candelabrum: “To cause a lamp to burn [ascend] continually” (Exodus 27:20) — that the flame should ascend on its own; consequently, in such a manner it is considered kindling. [This explanation was stated] in the name of Rabbi Isaac ha-Levi. And it is difficult to me: First, for Rami bar Ḥama taught it there [in Bameh Madlikin]; and furthermore, it is not a *baraita*, but rather he stated it as an explanation of another *mishnah*! And the rest of our teachers taught it regarding a bonfire [on Shabbat eve]. But I found it in *Torat Kohanim* regarding the candelabrum.

Rashi on Shabbat 20a:7:1.english: A single piece of wood - Similar to our wood stumps [coches].

Rashi on Shabbat 20a:7:2.english: Most of its thickness - That the fire should enter into its thickness up to most of it.

Rashi on Shabbat 20a:7:3.english: Most of its circumference - On the outside.

Rashi on Shabbat 20a:7:5.english: [So] that it is ruined - [This corresponds to] most of its thickness.

Rashi on Shabbat 20a:7:6.english: Both of its sides - [This corresponds to] most of its circumference.

Rashi on Shabbat 20a:7:7.english: An allusion to the matter - For thereafter it continues to burn.

Rashi on Shabbat 20a:7:8.hebrew: שני קצותיו אכלה האש - בידוע שתוכו נחר, והלכה לחה שלו ונעשה יבש:
Rashi on Shabbat 20a:7:8.english: The fire consumed both of its ends - It is certain that its middle is scorched, and its moisture is gone and it has become dry.

Rashi on Shabbat 20a:7:9.hebrew: נחר - פסק לחה שלה ויבש, כמו נחר גרוני (תהילים ס״ט:ד׳), וכן חרה מני חורב (איוב ל׳:ל׳):
Rashi on Shabbat 20a:7:9.english: Is burned - Its moisture ceased and it dried up, like “my throat is dried” (Psalms 69:4), and likewise, “is burned from heat” (Job 30:30).

Rashi on Shabbat 20a:8:1.english: And the hearth - It is written with regard to Jehoiakim's burning of the scroll.

Rashi on Shabbat 20a:8:2.hebrew: באחוה - כל העצים נדלקין זה מזה, הקטן מדליק הגדול:
Rashi on Shabbat 20a:8:2.english: In brotherhood - All the pieces of wood catch fire from one another, the small [piece] igniting the large [one].

Rashi on Shabbat 20a:9:1.hebrew: אין צריכין רוב - להצית את האור ברובן מע"ש, אלא מאחיז בהן אור מבעוד יום, לפי שאין כבין והולכים, אלא דולקים והולכים:
Rashi on Shabbat 20a:9:1.english: Do not require most - [That is, one is not required] to ignite the fire in most of them on Shabbat eve; rather, one [merely] sets fire to them while it is still day, because they do not progressively go out, but rather continue to burn.

Rashi on Shabbat 20a:9:2.english: [They] require most - Because the flame cannot enter between them.

Rashi on Shabbat 20a:9:3.hebrew: גרעינין - של תמרה. אם עשה מהם מדורה לכשיבשו, אין צריכין רוב:
Rashi on Shabbat 20a:9:3.english: Pits - Of dates. If he made a bonfire from them once they dried, they do not require [that] most [catch fire].

Rashi on Shabbat 20a:9:4.hebrew: נתנן בחותלות - כלים שעושין מלולבין, ונתן הכלי מלא במדורה — צריכין רוב, לפי שצבורין יחד, ואין השלהבת יכולה להכנס בהן:
Rashi on Shabbat 20a:9:4.english: [If] he placed them in baskets - [These are] vessels that are made from palm fronds; and [if] he placed the vessel full [of them] into the bonfire — they require most [to catch fire], because they are piled together, and the flame cannot enter into them.

Rashi on Shabbat 20a:9:5.hebrew: קנים מבדרן - לכאן ולכאן, ואחת מהן היוצאה לא תמצא את חברתה לבערה. הלכך, כי לא אגדן — צריכי רוב; אבל אגדן — לא מבדרן, ואין צריכין רוב. וכן גרעינין:
Rashi on Shabbat 20a:9:5.english: Reeds are scattered - Here and there, and one of them that sticks out will not find its fellow to ignite it. Therefore, when he did not tie them, they require most [to catch fire]; but [if] he tied them, they are not scattered, and they do not require most [to catch fire]. And so too with [date] seeds.

Tosafot on Shabbat 20a:3:1.hebrew: איבעיא להו תחתון האיך דגבי תנור - ולפ"ה דפי' דלגבי האור ממהר לקרום, ומיבעיא ליה: אם תחתון דקאמר ר' אליעזר דגבי תנור — והא דקאמרי רבנן "עד שיקרמו פניה", אחת מפניה, ואפילו בעליון סגי; ואם תחתון דקאמר ר"א היאך דגבי האור — אם כן, הא דקאמרי רבנן "עד שיקרמו פניה", היינו כל פניה. תא שמע: "ר' אליעזר כו'", ופושט דר"א לחומר'. ומיהו בירושלמי משמע דלהקל בא, דקאמר התם: "ומודה ר"א בלחם הפנים שאין קרוי לחם עד שיקרמו פניו בתנור". משמע דהכא סגי בקרימה כל דהו, אבל בלחם הפנים בעינן קרימה מעליא. ריב"א:
Tosafot on Shabbat 20a:3:1.english: "A dilemma was raised before them: Is the bottom that which is close to the oven?" - And according to the explanation of the Kuntres [Rashi], who explained that [the surface facing] toward the fire crusts more quickly, and the [Gemara's] dilemma is: If the "bottom" of which Rabbi Eliezer spoke is that which is close to the oven — and that which the Rabbis said, "until its surface forms a crust," [means] one of its surfaces, and even [crusting] on the upper [surface] is sufficient; whereas if the "bottom" of which Rabbi Eliezer spoke is that which is close to the fire — if so, that which the Rabbis said, "until its surface forms a crust," means all of its surfaces. "Come and hear: Rabbi Eliezer, etc." — and it resolves that Rabbi Eliezer [came] to be stringent. However, in the Yerushalmi it implies that he came to be lenient, for it says there: "And Rabbi Eliezer concedes regarding the Showbread that it is not called bread until its surface crusts in the oven." This implies that here [regarding Shabbat], any minimal crusting is sufficient, but regarding the Showbread, we require a substantial crusting. — RIBA [Rabbeinu Yitzchak ben Asher].

Tosafot on Shabbat 20a:5:1.hebrew: למשרי אברים ופדרים - וא"ת: אי אברים ופדרים דחול, כדפ"ה — הא אמר בפרק [במה מדליקין] (דף כד:): "עולת שבת בשבתו" — ולא עולת חול בשבת! ואי אברים ופדרים דשבת, ואשמועינן מ"בכל מושבותיכם", דאע"ג דמצותן כל הליל' ואפשר להקטירן במוצאי שבת, אפ"ה דחי שבת — הא מ"עולת שבת" נפק, מדממעט עולת חול, דהיינו ע"כ אברים ופדרים דחול, דשחיטה וזריק' עבר זמנו בשקיעת החמה; א"כ, אברים ופדרים דשבת קרבים בשבת! וי"ל: דאתי למשרי אברים ופדרים דחול כשמשלה בהן האור מבעוד יום. והא דקאמר "ולא עולת אברים ופדרי' דחול בשבת" — היינו דוקא בשלא משלה בהן האור. וכן הא דאמר בפרק טרף בקלפי (יומא דף מו. ושם): "אברי חול שנתותרו עושה להן מערכה בפני עצמן וסודרן אפי' בשבת" — ואפי' לרב הונא דפליג התם, היינו דאמר דאין עושה להן מערכה בפני עצמן, אבל ד"ה דסודרן על המערכה גדולה — היינו כשמשלה בהן האור, כדמוכח התם. והא דקאמר התם לחד לישנא דדוקא בפסולין, "אי משלה בהן האור — אין, אי לא — לא" — לאו משום דכשרים לא בעינן משלה בהן האור, אלא ה"ק: דדוקא בפסולים אצטריך לאשמעינן במשלה בהן האור, אבל בכשרים לא איצטריך לאשמעי'. וריב"א מסתפק בשאר קרבנות, כשמשלה בהן האור, אם נעשו כלחמו של מזבח למשרינהו בשבת אי לאו, דדילמא דוקא בתמיד מהני האי טעמא, משום דשם תמיד דוחה שבת. וקשה: דהתם מפיק ליה ביומא מ"במועדו" — ואפי' בשבת, והכא מפיק ליה מ"במושבותיכם"? ונראה, דעיקר דרשא מ"במושבותיכם", והתם נקט "במועדו ואפי' בשבת" אגב דבעי למנקט "במועדו ואפי' בטומאה". וע"ק: והא "במושבותיכם" אצטריך לשריפת בת כהן דלא דחיא שבת, כדדרשי' פ"ק דיבמות (דף ו: ושם) ופרק אחד דיני ממונות (סנהדרין לה:): "נאמר כאן במושבותיכם כו' אף מושבות האמור כאן כו'"! וי"ל: דהכא מ"כם" דריש, מדכתי' "מושבותיכם" ולא כתיב "מושבות". והא דדרשי' בפ"ק דקדושין (דף לז. ושם): "מושבות דכתב רחמנא גבי שבת ל"ל?", וקאמר דסד"א הואיל ובענין מועדות כתיב תבעי קדוש ב"ד כמועדות — קמ"ל — לא מ"לא תבערו אש בכל מושבותיכם" דריש, כדפירש הקונטרס, דההוא לא כתיבא בענין דמועדות, ואצטריך לה נמי כדדריש הכא; אלא "מושבותיכם" דכתי' באמור (ויקרא כ״ג:כ״א), דההוא כתיב בענינא דמועדות:
Tosafot on Shabbat 20a:5:1.english: To permit limbs and fats - And if you say: If [this refers to] limbs and fats of a weekday [offering], as Rashi explained — doesn't [the Gemara] say in the chapter [entitled] Bameh Madlikin (24b): "The burnt-offering of Shabbat on its Shabbat" — and not the burnt-offering of a weekday on Shabbat? And if [it refers to] limbs and fats of a Shabbat [offering], and [the verse] "in all your habitations" teaches us that even though their mitzvah [extends] the entire night and it is possible to burn them on Saturday night, even so it overrides Shabbat — doesn't this derive from "the burnt-offering of Shabbat," since it excludes the burnt-offering of a weekday? Which must perforce mean limbs and fats of a weekday [offering], since the time for slaughter and sprinkling [the blood of a weekday offering] has already passed by sunset; if so, the limbs and fats of a Shabbat [offering] are offered on Shabbat [night]! And one can say that [the verse] comes to permit limbs and fats of a weekday [offering] when the fire has already taken hold of them while it was still day. And that which [the Gemara] said, "and not the burnt-offering [consisting of] the limbs and fats of a weekday on Shabbat" — that is specifically when the fire had not taken hold of them. And similarly, that which was said in the chapter [entitled] Taraf BaKalpi (Yoma 46a and there): "Limbs of a weekday [offering] that were left over, one makes a separate arrangement [of wood] for them and arranges them even on Shabbat" — and even according to Rav Huna who disagrees there, that is [only] that he says that one does not make a separate arrangement for them, but all agree that one arranges them on the great arrangement — that is when the fire had already taken hold of them, as is demonstrated there. And that which was said there according to one version, that specifically regarding disqualified [sacrificial parts], if the fire took hold of them, yes, [they may remain on the altar], and if not, no — it is not because valid ones do not require that the fire have taken hold of them; rather, this is what it is saying: that specifically regarding disqualified ones it was necessary to teach us [the law] regarding [parts where] the fire took hold of them, but regarding valid ones it was not necessary to teach us. And the Riba is uncertain regarding other offerings when the fire took hold of them, whether they have become like "the bread of the altar" to permit them on Shabbat or not; for perhaps specifically regarding the daily offering (tamid) is this reasoning effective, because the classification of tamid overrides Shabbat. And it is difficult: for there in Yoma [45b], it derives it from "in its appointed season" — and even on Shabbat, whereas here it derives it from "in all your habitations"! And it appears that the primary derivation is from "in your habitations," and there it cited "in its appointed season — and even on Shabbat" incidentally, because it wanted to cite "in its appointed season — and even in ritual impurity." And furthermore it is difficult: wasn't "in your habitations" needed for [the execution by] burning of a priest's daughter, that it does not override Shabbat, as we expound in the first chapter of Yevamot (6b and there) and in the chapter [entitled] Echad Dinei Mamonot (Sanhedrin 35b): "It is stated here 'in your habitations'... just as 'habitations' stated here [means the court]..."? And one can say that here it expounds from [the suffix] "-khem" ("your"), since it is written "moshevoteikhem" and it is not written "moshavot." And as for that which we expound in the first chapter of Kiddushin (37a and there): "Why do I need 'habitations' that the Merciful One wrote regarding Shabbat?" and [the Gemara] says that you might have thought that since it is written in the context of the Festivals it would require sanctification by the court (kiddush Beit Din) like the Festivals, so it teaches us [that it does not] — it does not derive [this] from "You shall kindle no fire in all your habitations," as Rashi explained, for that [verse] is not written in the context of the Festivals, and it is also needed as it is expounded here; rather, [it derives this from] "your habitations" that is written in [Parashat] Emor (Leviticus 23:21), for that one is written in the context of the Festivals.

Tosafot on Shabbat 20a:6:1.hebrew: כדי שתהא שלהבת עולה מאיליה - אלמא, במקום שהקפיד הכתוב שלא יכבה, סגי שתהא שלהבת עולה מאליה, ואין צריך שתהא הפתילה שורפת ברובא:
Tosafot on Shabbat 20a:6:1.english: "So that the flame ascends on its own" - Evidently, in a case where Scripture was particular that it not go out, it suffices that the flame ascends on its own, and it is not necessary that the majority of the wick be burning.

Tosafot on Shabbat 20a:7:1.hebrew: עד שישחת ממלאכת האומן - אבל למ"ד משתאחוז האור משני צדדין, אינו נשחת בהכי ממלאכת האומן. ואע"ג דכתיב: "את שני קצותיו אכלה האש היצלח למלאכה" — היינו גבי עץ הגפן; אבל שאר עצים אין נשחתין כ"כ במהרה ממלאכת האומן:
Tosafot on Shabbat 20a:7:1.english: "Until it is ruined from the work of a craftsman" - However, according to the one who says [that it is sufficient] once the fire catches on both sides, [the wood] is not ruined from the work of a craftsman by this [alone]. And even though it is written: "The fire consumed both its ends... is it fit for any work?" [Ezekiel 15:4], that is regarding vine wood; but other woods are not ruined so quickly from the work of a craftsman.
